title_as_printed: Empirical data for the solubility of methane and ethane at 302oF in aqueous NaCl solutions at a salinity of 107 grams/liter.
pressure_note: column header 'psi'; absolute or gauge not stated for this table (difference <0.15% at 10,000-22,500 psi). Total system pressure over the CH4+C2H6 gas and brine; gas-phase composition not reported.

value.reference_state: SCF/Bbl: standard cubic feet of gas at 25 C (77 F) and 1 atm per barrel (42 US gal) of brine (report pages 15 and 19; Table A-2 footnote 'SCF at 25 C (77 F)')

value2.what: C2H6 dissolved, not printed; = Total Gas x (% C2H6)/100

pct_c2h6.unit: mole percent of the total dissolved gas
pct_c2h6.what: by gas chromatography (text p.51-52: 'mole percent ethane of the dissolved gas in solution'; Figure 14 axis 'MOLE PERCENT ETHANE')

ditto_fill_down: Ditto marks (") written as blank cells = same as the row above; fill down from the nearest printed value. Only row 1 has all values printed; T changes to 302 at sample 7, salinity to 105 at sample 11 and back to 107 at sample 19 (the title says 107 g/L for all), P to 10,000 at sample 15 and 9,980 at sample 25.
conversion_needs: Value is gas volume per barrel of brine (SCF at 25 C, 1 atm per 42-US-gal barrel). The authors analysed samples as mol gas per kg of SOLUTION and converted to SCF/Bbl 'using appropriate conversion factors' (report p.13) that are NOT given; the inverse conversion needs the brine density at 25 C (or at the authors' unstated reference) and the molar volume of ideal gas at 25 C, 1 atm (24.465 L/mol; 1 SCF = 28.3168 L; 1 bbl = 158.987 L). Whether 'barrel of brine' means brine volume at 25 C or at another temperature is not stated.

For orientation only, the report's comparison tables give the factors the authors used to turn literature mole fractions into SCF/Bbl: mole fraction = SCF/Bbl x 0.0001312 for pure water (Tables 4 and 5), 0.0001317 for 1 m NaCl and 0.0001328 for 4 m NaCl (Table 5). Basis of that mole fraction (salt counted or not) is not stated.
Salinity is g NaCl per litre of solution; conversion to molality needs solution density (not given). Text (report p.33) equates 52, 107, 167 g/L with 5, 10, 15 weight percent NaCl.
Temperature in F -> K: (F - 32)/1.8 + 273.15. Pressure psi -> MPa x 0.00689476.
C2H6 dissolved per sample = Total Gas x %C2H6/100 (or Total - CH4).
notes: 26 printed rows, 26 written; page 100 only (page 101 is Appendix B). Text p.51 says 26 measurements at 9 experimental conditions. Blank lines in the printed table (after samples 5, 10, 15, 20, 25) are layout only. Sample 6 is printed with two decimals (50.46, 48.19), kept. Sample 19: CH4 34.5 is inconsistent with Total 38.6 x (1 - 0.060) = 36.3 (all other rows agree within 0.1); kept as printed. Text (p.59) notes difficulty getting reproducible GC results, probably due to injection technique. 2026-10-11 coordinator: gas_mixture true (two dissolved gases); these rows belong to the ternary family, which the v1.2 builder cannot yet write, so the release excludes them until a ternary converter exists.
conversion_rule_note: Added 2026-10-11 (coordinator, approved by J. Moortgat): composition.density_rule nacl_25C_1atm converts g/L NaCl and SCF per barrel with the NaCl(aq) density at 298.15 K, 1 atm (gbb12_core.NACL_VPHI_25C); rows get the flag density-assumed.
